description: Sodium is a chemical element with symbol Na and atomic number 11. It is a soft, silvery-white, highly reactive metal and an alkali metal in group 1 of the periodic table. Its only stable isotope is 23Na, and the free metal does not occur in nature but must be prepared from compounds.
uses: Sodium compounds have immense commercial importance in industries producing glass, paper, soap, and textiles. Sodium hydroxide (lye) is used in soap manufacture, and sodium chloride (edible salt) serves as a de-icing agent and nutrient for animals including humans. Sodium is essential for all animals and some plants, playing a major role in maintaining extracellular fluid osmotic pressure and enabling nerve impulse transmission through the action potential.
characteristics: Sodium is a soft silvery metal at standard temperature and pressure that combines with oxygen in air to form sodium oxides, with a melting point of 98°C and boiling point of 883°C. It is a good conductor of electricity and heat, can be easily cut with a knife, and emits a characteristic yellow glow in flame tests due to excited 3s electrons. Sodium metal is highly reactive and reducing, reacting exothermically with water to produce caustic soda and flammable hydrogen gas.
